chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdallah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from more than one, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hasan ibn Jahm who said: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

A man from the Children of Israel had a son whom he loved greatly. He was visited in his sleep and it was said to him: 'Your son will die the night he enters upon his wife.' He said: When that night came, and he consummated the marriage, the father anticipated that [death] would happen, but he woke up finding his son healthy. His father came to him and said to him: 'O my son, did you do anything of good yesterday?' He said: 'No, except that a beggar came to the door and they had kept preserved for me some food, and I gave it to the beggar.' He (the father) said: 'Through this, Allah averted [death] from you.'

key_terms.يَدْخُلُ بِأَهْلِهِ: enters upon his wife (consummation of marriage)

ai.seo_question: How does charity alter divine decree in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This narrative from al-Kafi illustrates the concept of Bada' (divine change of decree) through a story of a man from the Children of Israel, linking the Imams' teachings to earlier prophetic traditions. Despite a vision predicting his son's death on his wedding night, the son's act of charity (giving away his reserved food to a beggar) caused Allah to avert the predicted death, demonstrating how good deeds can alter divine destiny. In Shia scholarship, this exemplifies how Bada' is not a change in God's knowledge but a manifestation of His will in response to specific conditions, such as charity or prayer, altering the apparent outcome of a decree.

en.ammaar-muslim: 8. [8/366] al-Kafi: Ali b. Muhammad b. Abdallah from Ahmad b. Muhammad from more than one from Ali b. Asbat from al-Hasan b. Jahm who said: Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام said: Abu Ja’farعليه السلام said:

A man from the Children of Israel had a son whom he used to love very much. He had a vision in his sleep and it was said to him: ‘Your son will die the very night that he enters upon his wife (i.e. on the wedding night)’. He (the Imam) said: when it was that night, and he consummated with her, the father believed that will happen, but he woke up finding his son well. His father came to him and said: O my son did you do anything of the good yesterday? He said: No. Except that a beggar came to the door and they had kept preserved for me some food and I gave it to the beggar. He (the father) said: Through this did Allah avert it (death) from you.
